Hi Laura / Mark — thanks again for the demo earlier today. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can get this into your security/procurement queue:

Call recap (high-level):
- Brightpath confirmed that several classes of generated output will be considered PII/PHI for your use case (patient names, limited clinical notes).
- You asked for explicit confirmation about what Redwood stores by default (prompts, user inputs, model outputs), where that data lives, and how long it is retained.
- You also asked about options to avoid storing prompts/outputs entirely (for an enterprise SLA / contract).

Can you confirm the two immediate items so we can prepare formal language for procurement:
1) Which environments are in scope for this proof-of-concept? (Hosted API in us-west preferred, or do you require EU residency?)
2) Do you need a written statement that Redwood will not retain prompt/output payloads beyond a contractual window (yes/no) or do you require an architecture move to Dedicated/Private?

I'll put together a short confirmation email from our security team addressing: what is stored by default, storage region options, default retention windows, and the contractual options for zero retention. If you need the DPA/SOC2 redacted report for procurement immediately, I can attach them in the follow-up.

Next steps:
- Please confirm environment (Hosted-us / Hosted-eu / Dedicated / Private) and whether you need the zero-retention contractual option.
- I'll follow up with a written confirmation from our security lead (Neha) by EOD Monday if possible.

Thanks,
Rishi

Hi Rishi — thanks for the recap. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Environment: For the POC we prefer Hosted-eu (data residency in EU) because we'll be testing EU patient data subsets. If Hosted-eu is not available for the POC, we can do Hosted-us with strict isolation but procurement will flag it.
2) Retention: We consider prompt+output payloads to be sensitive (PII/PHI). Procurement/security have asked that we get a written statement that outlines exactly what Redwood stores by default and what contractual options exist to avoid storing prompt/output payloads (we may require zero retention or Private deployment).

Can you confirm the exact default retention windows, which artifacts are stored (raw prompt text, model output, and any derived embeddings or summaries), and whether logs/metadata used for billing are separate?

We need a short, formal note we can share with our Head of Security and procurement. If you can provide that plus SOC2 & DPA, we'll start the review. Ideally we need this by EOD Thursday so procurement can kick off review next week.

Thanks,
Laura Jensen
Head of Data Security, Brightpath Health

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: PII handling — prompt/output storage confirmation

Laura — thanks, helpful. Below is a concise summary you can share internally. Neha from our security team will send a formal confirmation and attach the DPA/SOC2 redacted report.

Short formal summary (what Redwood stores & options):
- Hosted (default):
  - Stored artifacts: full request payloads (prompt/user input) and model responses (outputs) are stored encrypted at rest by default. These are retained for 30 days to support debugging, quality investigations, and allow customers to opt-in to long-term analytics.
  - Metadata & billing records: request metadata (timestamps, token counts, model id, routing decisions) are retained for 13 months to support billing, usage analytics, and abuse detection. Metadata does not include full prompt text.
  - Region: Hosted endpoints are provisioned per-region; we can run your POC in Hosted-eu (EU data residency) for the duration of the trial.
- Dedicated:
  - Dedicated capacity runs in a customer-dedicated project/VPC. By default, prompts/outputs can be configured to follow the same 30-day retention, but we offer an option to disable prompt/output persistence (zero retention) for request payloads. Billing metadata retention (13 months) remains unless otherwise contracted.
- Private (on-prem/VPC):
  - In Private deployments the customer controls storage; by default no payloads are exported to Redwood-managed backups and retention can be set to 0 days. Key management can be integrated with customer KMS.

Additional notes:
- Encryption: Data is encrypted in transit (TLS) and at rest (AES-256). We support customer-managed keys for Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Access & audit: Access to request payloads is restricted to authorized SRE/security staff; audit logs capture access and are available under SOC2 controls.
- Contractual option: We can commit to a contract clause for zero-persistence of prompt/output payloads on Dedicated/Private deployments (we'll draft language for procurement). For Hosted, zero-persistence is possible via an account-level opt-out but may limit support/observability features.

Attachments: I'll attach the DPA and redacted SOC2 report in the next email for procurement.

Does this work for you to circulate? Happy to tighten language for procurement wording.

Thanks,
Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Formal: PII handling — prompt/output storage (Redwood confirmation)

Hi Laura / Mark — Neha from Redwood Security here. Following Rishi's summary, a formal confirmation below you can share with procurement/security. Attached: Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf (DPA), SOC2_report_redacted.pdf (control summary).

Official confirmation (summary):
- Scope of stored data (Hosted default):
  - Full request payloads (raw prompt text / user input) and model outputs are by default persisted encrypted at rest for 30 days. Persistence supports debugging, ephemeral rollbacks, and opt-in analytics.
  - Derived artifacts (embeddings, reranks) are treated as derived data; retention follows the same policy unless specifically excluded.
  - Metadata (billing, token usage, routing) is retained for 13 months and does not include full prompt or output text.
- Residency:
  - We operate regional Hosted endpoints. For your POC we can provision Hosted-eu so all stored artifacts for the POC remain in the EU region.
- Encryption & keys:
  - TLS in transit and AES-256 at rest. Dedicated/Private deployments support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM).
- Access controls & audit:
  - Role-based access control, just-in-time access reviews, and immutable audit logs of accesses to request payloads. SOC2 control mapping included in the attached report.
- Contractual & operational options:
  - Dedicated deployment: option to disable prompt/output persistence (zero retention) via configuration + contractual commitment.
  - Private/on-prem: customer controls storage and retention; by default no Redwood-managed persistence is exported.
  - Hosted with opt-out: we can implement an account-level opt-out for prompt/output persistence for Hosted customers; this will be included in a procurement addendum and may affect observability features.

If procurement/security needs stricter language (for example, "Redwood will not retain prompt/response payloads beyond X hours/days"), we can propose specific contractual text and a related verification plan (quarterly audits / SOC2 supplement).

Please let me know any follow-up items you need and I'll coordinate the DPA/SOC2 bundle and the procurement addendum.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
